situation_en: Fill out a lifestyle questionnaire for a school survey. Write each question and your answer (you can invent the answers): how many hours you sleep, how often you exercise, what you eat for breakfast and what you do to relax.
Write a post about your local park: what you can do there, who goes there and why it is good for people’s routines.
A friend wants to start a healthier routine. Send messages to invite your friend to exercise with you: say where and when, and ask what your friend likes to do.
Write an email to a friend about a small habit you want to change, such as phone use, sleep or study time: what it is, why and what you will do.
Write a notice for a school competition: what the competition is, who can enter, when and where it is and how to sign up.
Explain the rules of a sport or game you know to a beginner: the goal, three rules and one thing that is not allowed.
Fill out the membership form for a club (sports, music or chess). Write each item and your answer (you can invent the details): name, age, experience and why you want to join.
Write a review of a sports event or a competition you watched on TV or in person, or imagine one: what happened, the best moment and your opinion.
Write a short report about how the students in your class travel to school: the question you ask, the results and one conclusion. Invent the results of a survey of five classmates.
Plan a day trip with friends. Send messages: how to get there, what time to meet and what to bring.
Write advice for a visitor on how to use public transportation in your city or in a city you know: tickets, best times to travel and one tip.
Write a paragraph about your favorite way to travel: start with a topic sentence and give two reasons.
Write a short story about a challenge: who the person is, what the challenge is, what happens and how it ends. Use the simple past.
Write an email to a friend about a challenge you completed, such as a race, a test or a project: what it was, what was difficult and how you felt.
Write a post about something you learned to do, such as a skill or a hobby: how you practiced, who helped you and what you learned.
Take notes to retell a story you know, from a book, a film or your own life: who, where and what happened. Then write the ending.
Write a formal email to a company: you ordered a reusable bottle three weeks ago and it has not arrived. Say what you ordered, when you ordered it and what you want the company to do.
Write a notice for your school about recycling: where to put each kind of trash and one rule.
Write a short report about how much plastic you use in one day: the items, the amounts and one idea to use less. Estimate or invent the amounts.
Write an email to a friend to invite them to a clean-up day in a park: when, where and what to bring.
Describe a celebration you know: when it happens, what people do, what they wear and why it is special.
Write two messages about a party: one that invites a friend and one that politely says no to an invitation.
Write an email inviting a friend from another country to visit during a local festival: when it is, what happens and why your friend will like it.
Write a post about a ceremony or a tradition for an important moment in life, such as a graduation or a birthday: what happens and why it matters.
Write a résumé for a part-time job, such as in a café, a library or tutoring: contact, education, experience, skills and languages. Invent the details.
Write a job ad for a school event: the job, the days, the hours and the skills people need.
A friend has a job interview tomorrow. Send messages with advice: what to wear, what to say and what to ask.
Write a profile of a famous person with an interesting job, or of an influencer you know about: what they do and why people follow them.
Write one paragraph about an invention you would like to see: begin with a topic sentence, give two reasons and end with a closing sentence.
Explain to a beginner how to use an app or a machine you know well, step by step.
Write a review of a gadget or an app that you use: what it does, what is good, what is bad and your rating from 1 to 5 stars.
Write an email to your school to ask if a robotics club can start: why, what students will do and what you need.
Write a review of a product you use every day, such as shoes, a bottle or a phone case: what it is, what you like, what could be better and whether you recommend it.
Write an ad for a famous product from your country, such as a food, a drink or a brand: its name, what makes it special and where to buy it.
Describe a logo you remember well, such as a brand or a team: the colors, the shapes and what it makes you think of.
Your friend writes: “Should I buy the red backpack or the black one?” Send messages: choose one and give two reasons.
You received this email from a friend: “I’m going to visit your city in July. What should I see? Where should I stay?” Write a reply with suggestions.
Write a polite email to a hotel about a problem, real or imagined: the room was not clean when you arrived. Say what the problem is and what you want.
Write a review of a place you visited, on vacation or in your city: what you did, what was good and what could be better.
Write a short blog post about a problem on a trip, such as lost luggage, bad weather or a missed bus, and how you solved it.

Write a short biography of a person who changed history, such as an inventor, an explorer or a scientist: when and where the person was born, key events and why the person is important. Write what you remember; exact dates are not necessary.
Write a short story about someone who finds a message in a bottle on a beach: who finds it, what the message says and what happens next.
Describe an old object, real or imagined, such as a coin, a map or a toy: who used it and what people did with it.
Write an email to a friend about a museum or a historical place that you visited or want to visit.
Write an article for the school website about an animal or a plant, real or well known: a headline, an introduction, one paragraph and a closing sentence.
Write a short report about water use at your school: the question, the results and one idea to save water. Invent the results.
Describe a nature scene you remember or imagine: what is in it, what colors you see and how you feel.
Write a post asking people to protect a natural place near you: what the place is, what the problem is and what people can do.
